info.title: Watermark API
info.summary: Watermark, resize and convert images, videos and PDFs.
info.description:
Send a file and a list of operations; the API processes the file in the background and returns a link to the result. Built for jobs a local script does badly: batches of hundreds of files, video, PDF and Word documents that keep their type, HEIC and camera RAW photos, text in real fonts, and delivery straight to your own S3 bucket.

The file is a public URL, an upload (`POST /v1/uploads`, for a file that is not on the web), a file an earlier request made (`file_…`) or an object in a connected bucket. Never send a file's bytes in a request body.

Every processing endpoint answers `202` with a request in status `queued`; send `wait` (up to 25 seconds) to get `200` with the finished request when it is quick. Otherwise poll `GET /v1/requests/{id}` or pass `webhook_url`. Download `result.files[0].url`; failed requests are free.

Many files with the same operations go through one `POST /v1/batches`, paced by the account and zipped at the end. `POST /v1/previews` shows what operations will do on one file before you run them. A `template` (`POST /v1/templates`) keeps an operations list, and the logo it uses, on the account for every call after.

**[See every operation, with the request to send and a picture of the result](https://api.watermark.ws/docs/operations)**

Docs: https://api.watermark.ws/docs · For AI agents: https://api.watermark.ws/docs/agents · As Markdown: https://api.watermark.ws/llms.txt

tags.name: Images
tags.description: Watermark, resize, crop, filter, draw text and convert photos, one or hundreds at a time. JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, TIFF, BMP, HEIC, AVIF, SVG, PSD and camera RAW in; JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, TIFF or BMP out.

tags.name: Videos
tags.description: Watermark every frame, resize, crop, rotate and re-encode, or save one frame as an image. MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, AVI, FLV, WMV, MPEG and MPEG-TS in; MP4, MOV, M4V, MKV, WebM, AVI, MPEG, FLV or WMV out. Needs an account that has bought credits.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: Watermark every page, or render one page as an image. PDF and Word (DOCX) in; a PDF stays a PDF and a Word file a Word file. Snapshots are images.

tags.name: Previews
tags.description: See what operations will do before running them: one small picture of a photo, a frame of a video or a page of a document, usually made within the call, with where each watermark landed.

tags.name: Batches
tags.description: Process many files with one operations list in one call. The files run a few at a time, by position, under the account's `batch_concurrency`; each is an ordinary request, and the results can be zipped or written to a prefix of your bucket.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: An operations list kept on the account under a name, with the logo it uses kept as long as it is. Send its id as `template` on any processing endpoint, a batch or a preview instead of, or before, `operations`.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: The files requests made: read, download and delete them.

tags.name: Uploads
tags.description: Upload a file to the API for a request to read, when it is not on the web: a file in your workspace, attached to a chat or on the user's computer.

tags.name: Storage
tags.description: Connect a bucket of your own, so requests read from it and results are delivered into it instead of through a download link.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Balance, usage and the operation catalog.

post.description: Get a URL to upload a file to, then send the upload's id as a request's `source`. The first request that succeeds uses it up and the file is deleted; a request that fails leaves it for a retry. Unused uploads are deleted after a day.

content_type.description: Such as `image/heic`, `video/mp4` or `application/pdf`. The PUT must send the same.

201.description: The upload, with its PUT URL.

get.description: An upload's status, with a fresh PUT URL while nothing has been uploaded.

delete.description: Delete an upload no request is using.

post.description: Connect an S3 bucket of yours. Create an IAM role that may read and write under the prefixes you list, give it the returned `trust_policy`, then verify the connection. The API assumes the role with the `external_id` it made for this connection, so no other account can use your role. Accounts that have bought credits only.

prefixes.description: Key prefixes ending in `/`; requests may only use keys under these.

201.description: The connection, unverified, with its policies.

patch.description:
Change the prefixes, or whether the connection may read or write; the bucket, region and role stay. Send the whole new list of prefixes. The API checks the new settings as verify does before keeping them, so a connection requests use only changes to settings your role allows: give the role the new permissions first, such as an added prefix, then send the change. The response has the `permissions_policy` the role now needs; remove what it no longer lists.

If the check fails, the answer is a `422` with the check's code (as verify's) and, in `error.permissions_policy`, the policy the new settings need. A verified connection is then left as it was. One that was not verified yet takes the new settings and becomes `failed`, as a failed verify leaves it.

prefixes.description: The whole new list of key prefixes, each ending in `/`.

read.description: Whether requests may read through the connection.

write.description: Whether requests may write through the connection.

200.description: The connection, verified with its new settings.

delete.description: Requests can no longer use the connection. Nothing in the bucket is touched.

post.description: The API assumes your role, then under each prefix writes, reads back and deletes a small object, as the connection allows. Requests can use it once verified; a failure says why in `last_error`.
Stop a request that has not finished. It is not charged.

200.description: The aborted request. One that has already finished is a `409 request_finished`.

get.description: The account's finishing events since a moment, oldest first, as their webhooks carried them (or would have). Catch up after your receiver was down, instead of polling every request. Kept for 30 days.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events after this moment, ISO 8601.

200.description: The events. With `has_more`, ask again from the last one's `created`.

get.description: The account behind the key: balance, tier, and the key's mode and limits.
Requests, spend and bytes over at most 92 days, grouped by day, endpoint, customer or status.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to 29 days ago.

get.description: The built-in fonts a `text` operation can name in `font`. Your own font goes in `font_url` instead.
Every operation, its parameters and the output formats, per media type: what a client needs to build requests. The same catalog, with pictures, is at https://api.watermark.ws/docs/operations.

200.description: The catalog. The example shows one operation of one media type.

resize.description: Resize to a width and height.

preserve_aspect_ratio.description: Fit inside the box instead of stretching to it.

crop_center.description: Fill the box and crop what overflows, centered.

post.description:
One small picture of what operations, or a template, will do to a file: the photo, one frame of a video (`at`) or one page of a document (`page`), reduced to `width` pixels wide, with the operations run on that copy. Pixel arguments are scaled down with it; `anchor`, `margin`, `size` and other percentages need nothing. It waits by default (`wait` 20) and usually runs within the call, so the answer carries the picture: `result.files[0]` is a WebP kept for a day, and `result.data.layout` says where each watermark and text landed, in the preview's pixels, for drawing handles over it.

Price: {{price:previews}} per request. Failed requests are free.

200.description: Finished within `wait`: the preview, with its picture and layout.

202.description: Not finished within `wait` (or `wait` was 0): follow it with `GET /v1/requests/{id}`.

post.description:
Run one operations list, or a template, on many files. Every source is checked and the whole batch priced before it is accepted: a prepaid account must hold the estimate (files × the endpoint's price, × outputs), and a test key counts each file toward its requests a day. The files then run as ordinary requests, `batch_concurrency` at a time by position, charged as each succeeds; they do not count against `concurrent_requests`. When the last one is done the hold is released, the results are zipped into parts of at most 4 GB or 1,000 files if `zip` was sent, and `batch.finished` is posted to `webhook_url`.

Price: each file costs its media's process price (`images/process`, `videos/process` or `documents/process`), and each further output the price of processing an image. Failed and aborted files are free.

202.description: Accepted: the batch, `queued`, with its counts and the estimate it holds.

200.description: The batch first sent with this Idempotency-Key (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only batches older than this id. Pass the last id of a page to get the next one.

get.description: One batch, with its counts, `progress` and, once finished with `zip`, its `zips`. With `wait`, the answer comes when the batch finishes or the wait runs out, so a script can follow a batch without polling.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the batch to finish before answering.

get.description: The batch's files as requests, by `position`: each with its status, its result or its error. Filter by `status` to find the failed ones; page with `after`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only requests after this `position`. Pass the last position of a page to get the next one.

200.description: A page of the batch's requests, in position order.

error.message: The source could not be downloaded: 404 Not Found.

post.description: Run the failed files of a finished batch again, as new requests at the same positions. The batch goes back to `processing`; its zips are built again when it finishes. A batch still running is a `409 batch_not_finished`; one with no failed file a `409 nothing_to_retry`.
Stop a batch: files still waiting never run and running ones are aborted, none of them charged; files already done keep their results. A finished batch is a `409 batch_finished`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only templates made before this one. Pass the last id of a page to get the next one.

post.description: Keep an operations list under a name. The operations are checked as a request's would be, for the template's `media` (`any` is checked as an image). A watermark whose `image` is an upload (`upl_…`) or a file (`file_…`) is copied into an asset of the template, which lasts as long as the template does, and the operation then names the asset; an `image_url` stays a URL. An account may keep `max_templates` (`422 too_many_templates` past that). Needs the `templates` scope; using a template needs only `process`.

patch.description: Change the name, the media or the operations; what is left out stays. New operations are checked for the media as on create. An upload or file they name becomes an asset, and an asset no operation names any more is deleted. Requests already running keep the operations they started with.

delete.description: Delete a template and the assets it kept. Requests that named it keep running; new ones get a `404 template_not_found`.

post.description: A request finished with a result. Signed in the `Watermark-Signature` header: `t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with your webhook secret>`.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried 3 times.

post.description: A request finished without a result; it is not charged. Signed in the `Watermark-Signature` header: `t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with your webhook secret>`.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried 3 times.

post.description: A request was aborted. Signed in the `Watermark-Signature` header: `t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with your webhook secret>`.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried 3 times.

post.description: A request moved on while it runs: `progress`, `stage` or `runtime` changed. Only when the request asked for it in `events`; at most one every 2 seconds, and only once progress moved 5 points. Signed in the `Watermark-Signature` header: `t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with your webhook secret>`.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried 3 times.

post.description: A batch finished: `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed` or `aborted`, with its counts, its price and, when asked for, its zips. The files of a batch send no events of their own unless the batch set `request_events`. Signed in the `Watermark-Signature` header: `t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with your webhook secret>`.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried 3 times.

post.description: A batch's files moved on: sent every 5% of files finished, when the batch asked for it in `events`. Signed in the `Watermark-Signature` header: `t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with your webhook secret>`.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried 3 times.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: the same key with the same body returns the first request instead of starting another.

ImageOperationResize.title: resize
ImageOperationResize.description: Resize to a width and height.

preserve_aspect_ratio.description: Fit inside the box instead of stretching to it.

crop_center.description: Fill the box and crop what overflows, centered.

x.description: Left edge in pixels. Below 0, the rectangle starts outside the file and only the part inside is kept.

y.description: Top edge in pixels. Below 0, the rectangle starts outside the file and only the part inside is kept.

ImageOperationRotate.title: rotate
ImageOperationRotate.description: Rotate by degrees, clockwise, optionally mirror, and level or straighten the perspective.

straighten.description: A further turn, in degrees, to level a tilted horizon. `images/read` with `level` suggests it.

lean_vertical.description: Correct converging verticals: how far the bottom (positive) or the top (negative) is drawn in, as a percent of the width, -50 to 50.

lean_horizontal.description: Correct converging horizontals: how far the right side (positive) or the left (negative) is drawn in, as a percent of the height, -50 to 50.

corners.description: What happens to the corners levelling uncovers: `crop` zooms in just enough to hide them, `color` fills them with corner_color, `blur` fills them with a blurred copy of the image. `fill` means `color`.

corner_color.description: The fill for uncovered corners when corners is `color`. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

ImageOperationBorder.title: border
ImageOperationBorder.description: Add a border of a color on each side.

color.description: The border color. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

ImageOperationWatermark.title: watermark
ImageOperationWatermark.description: Place an image (a logo, usually a transparent PNG) over the file. Say where with `anchor` and `margin`, or with `x` and `y` in pixels; `size`, `opacity` and `rotation` prepare the image on the way.

image_url.description: URL of the watermark image (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP). Send this or `image`.

image.description: The watermark image as a file an earlier request made (`file_…`) or an object in your connected bucket. Send this or `image_url`.

anchor.description: Where the watermark sits: top_left, top, top_right, left, center, right, bottom_left, bottom, bottom_right. Send this or `x` and `y`.

margin.description: How far in from the anchored edges: pixels, or a percentage of the shorter side ("3%").

size.description: The watermark's width: pixels, or a percentage of the file's width ("18%"); the height follows. Left out, it goes on at its own size.

opacity.description: Opacity of the watermark, 0-100; 100 leaves it as it is.

rotation.description: Turn the watermark by degrees, clockwise.

tile_spacing.description: Repeat the watermark across the whole file, starting at the top-left margin: the step from one copy to the next, pixels or a percentage of the width ("25%").

x.description: The x position in pixels, from the top left. Send `anchor` instead to place it relative to the file.

y.description: The y position in pixels, from the top left.

tile_spacing_x.description: Repeat the watermark across the file: the step in pixels from one copy's left edge to the next (with tile_spacing_y).

tile_spacing_y.description: When tiling, the step in pixels from one copy's top edge to the next.

diagonal_lines_color.description: Also draw two diagonal lines corner to corner in this color. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

ImageOperationThumbnail.title: thumbnail
ImageOperationThumbnail.description: Make a small, fast-loading copy, metadata stripped.

width.description: The width in pixels; kept in proportion when left out. Send this, `height` or both.

height.description: The height in pixels; kept in proportion when left out.

strip_animation.description: Keep only the first frame of an animated GIF or WebP: a much smaller still preview.

ImageOperationSepia.title: sepia
ImageOperationSepia.description: Give the image a sepia tone.

name.description: One of: amaro, apollo, brannan, earlybird, gotham, hefe, inkwell, kelvin, lomo, nashville, poprocket, rise, sierra, toaster, valencia, walden, willow, xpro2.

ImageOperationRemoveBackground.title: remove_background
ImageOperationRemoveBackground.description: Make the background color transparent (output PNG or WebP to keep it).

tolerance.description: How far from the background color still counts as background, 0-100.

ImageOperationOrient.title: orient
ImageOperationOrient.description: Turn the image upright from its EXIF orientation.

ImageOperationText.title: text
ImageOperationText.description: Draw text on the image, in a built-in font or your own.

text.description: The text. A line break starts a new line.

size.description: The font size: pixels, or a percentage of the image's width ("4%").

margin.description: How far in from the anchored edges: pixels, or a percentage of the shorter side ("2%"). Added to x and y.

color.description: The text color. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

position.description: Where x and y are measured from: top_left, top, top_right, left, center, right, bottom_left, bottom, bottom_right.

x.description: Offset from the position, in pixels.

y.description: Offset from the position, in pixels.

font.description: A built-in font by name, from `GET /v1/fonts`. Send this or `font_url`.

font_url.description: Your own TrueType, OpenType or WOFF font, by URL.

ImageOperationTrim.title: trim
ImageOperationTrim.description: Cut away edges of one flat color, such as the empty canvas around text.

fuzz.description: How far from the edge color still counts as it, in percent: 0 for exactly that color, more for paper or noise.

ImageOperationColor.title: color
ImageOperationColor.description: Adjust brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth and tint, or tone it mono or sepia.

auto.description: Fix levels and color balance automatically first.

ImageOperationFrame.title: frame
ImageOperationFrame.description: Put the image in a frame: a border, a mat, an instant print, film, a caption bar and more.

style.description: One of: border, mat, instant, exif, film, float, fade, bevel, stamp, torn, shape, album, rounded, shadow, fit.

color.description: The frame color. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

size.description: Frame width, as a percent of the shorter side.

mat_color.description: The mat or inner color. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

edge.description: Edge width, as a percent of the shorter side.

bottom.description: Extra space below, as a percent of the shorter side.

radius.description: Corner radius, as a percent of the shorter side.

ratio.description: For `fit`: the shape to pad to, such as "4:5" or "1.91:1".

blur.description: For `fit` and `float`: fill with a blurred copy of the image.

gradient_color.description: For `border`: blend the frame to this color. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

angle.description: For `border`: the gradient's angle. For `instant`: the print's tilt, -15 to 15 degrees.

line_color.description: For `mat`: a fine line inside the mat. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

text_color.description: For `exif` and `film`: the text color. A hex color, such as "#ffffff" or "#fff".

shape.description: For `shape`: arch, circle or oval. For `fade`: oval or rectangle.

prefix.description: A key prefix ending in `/`, under one of the connection's prefixes.

media.description: What every source is. Video needs an account that has bought credits.

sources.description: The files, at most your account's `batch_max_files` (`422 batch_too_large` past that): each a public URL, an upload, a file an earlier request made, an object in your bucket, or every object under a prefix of it. See [Sources](https://api.watermark.ws/docs/files.md#sources).

template.description: A template to run first (`tpl_…`, from `POST /v1/templates`): its operations, then the request's own, if any. A template made for another media is a `422 template_media_mismatch`. See [Templates](https://api.watermark.ws/docs/templates.md).

operations.description: Run on every file, for the `media`. Required, unless `template` is sent.

items.description: An operation of the media in question; `type` picks which.

output.description: How to save each result: the same as one output named `result`.

format.description: A format of the `media`, such as `webp`, `mp4` or `pdf`; the media's first format when left out. See [Operations](https://api.watermark.ws/docs/operations.md).

outputs.description: Several files per source, as on a single request, each costing the price of processing an image after the first. No output may have a `destination` of its own: the batch's `destination` holds every file.

name.description: Your name for it, unique in the batch, such as `web` or `thumb`; part of each file's name.

items.description: An operation of the media in question; `type` picks which.

operations.description: Run after the shared operations, for this output only.

destination.description: Write every file into your bucket instead of keeping it: `prefix` + the source's name (+ `-` + the output's name, with `outputs`) + `.` + the format. Accounts that have bought credits only; not with `zip`.

storage.description: A verified storage connection that may write (`stg_…`).

prefix.description: A key prefix ending in `/`, under one of the connection's prefixes.

zip.description: Also zip the results when the batch finishes, in parts of at most 4 GB or 1,000 files each, listed in `zips`. Not with `destination`.

max_duration.description: Videos: only keep the first this many seconds of each.

max_pages.description: Documents: only keep the first this many pages of each.

webhook_url.description: Where to post the batch when it finishes (`batch.finished`), and its progress if asked for. Defaults to the account's webhook, if set. See [Webhooks](https://api.watermark.ws/docs/webhooks.md).

events.description: The batch events to post: `batch.finished` when it is done, `batch.progress` every 5% of files finished.

request_events.description: Events to post for each file as well, as single requests send them. None by default: the files of a batch are quiet.

customer.description: Your own reference, kept on the batch and on each of its requests.

metadata.description: Up to 20 keys of your own, kept on the batch and on each of its requests.

status.description: `queued` until its files are created, `processing` while they run, `zipping` while the zips are written; then `succeeded` (every file did), `partial` (some failed or were aborted), `failed` (none succeeded) or `aborted`.

progress.description: Files finished, as a percentage of `counts.total`.

input.description: What was sent: the template, the operations, the output, the destination, `max_duration`, `max_pages` and `zip`, those that were.

template.description: The template's id, when one was sent.

destination.description: The `storage` and `prefix`, when the files go to your bucket.

price.description: What the batch has cost so far: each file is charged as it succeeds. Until it finishes, `estimate_micro_usd` is what the whole batch would cost, which a prepaid account holds.

estimate_micro_usd.description: While unfinished: the estimate held for the batch, in millionths of a dollar.

zips.description: Once a batch sent with `zip` has finished: the zip parts, each a file with a download link and `files`, how many results it holds. Kept 7 days, like the results.

files.description: How many files the part holds.

requests.description: Where to list the batch's files as requests: `GET /v1/batches/{id}/requests`.

error.description: When the batch itself went wrong, apart from its files: `code` and `message`, such as a zip that could not be built.

media.description: What the template is for. `any` suits every endpoint, so its operations must be ones every media takes, such as `watermark`.

items.description: An operation of the media in question; `type` picks which.

operations.description: The operations, as a request sends them. A watermark's `image` may be an upload (`upl_…`) or a file (`file_…`): it is copied into an asset the template keeps, and the stored operation names the asset. See [Operations](https://api.watermark.ws/docs/operations.md).

media.description: What the template is for; its operations must suit it.

items.description: An operation of the media in question; `type` picks which.

operations.description: The whole new list. Name an existing asset by its `file_…` id to keep it; an asset no operation names is deleted.

id.description: Starts `tpl_`. Send it as `template` on a processing endpoint, a batch or a preview.

livemode.description: `false` for a template made with a test key.

operations.description: The operations as kept: an upload or file sent as a watermark's `image` has become the id of one of `assets`.

assets.description: The files the template keeps, for as long as it exists.

endpoint.description: Which endpoint started it, such as `images/process`; `previews` for a preview.

status.description: Where the request is. Only `succeeded` is charged. `waiting` is a file of a batch that has not been let go yet.

source.description: The source as sent: a URL, a file id, or a storage object.

batch.description: For a file of a batch: the batch's id.

position.description: For a file of a batch: its place in `sources`, from 0.

input.description: What was sent besides the source: operations, output and the endpoint's own fields.

stage.description: While unfinished: waiting its turn in a batch, waiting for a worker, waiting for a long-video worker to start (about a minute), or being worked on.

runtime.description: Where it runs, once started: `inline` while you waited, `standard` on a queue worker, `extended` on a worker for long videos.

progress.description: How far a video has got while it is processing.

data.description: About the output: dimensions and format for images, duration and codec for videos, pages and size for PDFs.

files.description: The files made, one per output, in the order the outputs were sent. Read endpoints make none.

deleted_at.description: When the first file is deleted. Each file has its own `deleted_at`.

partial.description: On a failed request: the files listed were written before the output that failed.

output.description: The output that could not be written, when that was the failure.

retryable.description: Whether sending the same request again may succeed: true when a file or place it writes to could not be reached, or when processing stopped through no fault of the file.

breakdown.description: With more than one output: what each output cost. The first costs the endpoint's price, each further one the price of processing an image.

Upload.description: A file uploaded for a request to read.

id.description: Starts `upl_`. Send it as a request's `source`.

status.description: `pending` until the file is uploaded; `in_use` while a request reads it; `consumed` once one succeeded.

upload.description: While `pending`: PUT the file here, with these headers, before `expires_at`. Get the upload again for a fresh URL.

expires_at.description: The upload is deleted then if no request has used it.

StorageObject.description: An object in your bucket, through a storage connection that may read.

key.description: The object key, under one of the connection's prefixes.

prefixes.description: The only keys it may read or write start with one of these.

external_id.description: Made by the API for this connection. Your role's trust policy must require it.

trust_policy.description: The trust policy to give the role, as is.

permissions_policy.description: The least the role needs on the bucket.

request.description: The request that made it. Only from `GET /v1/files/{id}`.

data.description: Its dimensions; a video's duration, a document's pages.

url.description: A signed link to download it, with no key, until it is deleted. Anyone with the link can download the file. Only for files the API keeps.

destination.description: For a file written to your own storage: `storage` and `key`, or the presigned `url` without its signature; and its `etag`.

url_expires_at.description: When the link stops working: when the file is deleted.

deleted_at.description: When the file is, or was, deleted.

billing.description: `prepaid`: requests use credit bought ahead. `invoiced`: charges are billed later, up to `credit_limit`.

limits.description: What the key runs with: its tier's limits, or the account's own where it has them.

concurrent_requests.description: How many of the account's requests may be queued or processing at once.

concurrent_extended.description: Of those, how many may run on the long-video workers at once.

max_operations.description: The most operations one request, or one output, may list.

batch_max_files.description: The most files one batch may hold.

batch_concurrency.description: How many files of the account's batches run at once, apart from `concurrent_requests`.

max_templates.description: How many templates the account may keep.

requests_per_day.description: Test keys only. A batch's files each count as one.

id.description: The same on every retry of a delivery. Use it to ignore a repeat.

data.description: The request as `GET /v1/requests/{id}` returns it; for a `batch.*` event, the batch as `GET /v1/batches/{id}` returns it.

error.message: The operations.0.width field must be between 1 and 20000.

param.description: The input the error is about.

errors.description: Every invalid field, for a validation error.

permissions_policy.description: For a storage change whose check failed: the permissions policy the new settings need.

401.description: No key, or not a valid one.

402.description: No credit left, or not enough for the whole batch, or the endpoint needs an account that has paid.

403.description: Not allowed: the key lacks the scope, the account is suspended or may not use the feature, or the storage connection may not read or write there.

409.description: A conflict: the request or batch has finished, there is nothing to retry, or the Idempotency-Key was used for another request.

422.description: Invalid input, or a URL the API will not use.

429.description: Too many requests a minute (rate_limited, see Retry-After), or too many of the account's requests running at once (concurrency_limited).
